subject: Intermittent partial-response dropouts on streaming endpoint
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@acme-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T16:12:00Z
Subject: Spike in partial responses from /v1/stream (production)

Monica / Redwood team,

We started seeing a higher error/partial-response rate on our production streaming integration around 09:05 PDT. ~4-6% of streaming responses are arriving truncated mid-response (client-side notices connection closed mid-frame), which causes our downstream processors to treat them as failures. This is triggering retries and backpressure spikes on our pipeline.

Samples and a pcap are attached — you can see repeated sequences where the stream ends with an unexpected FIN while payload appears incomplete. Some requests return 200 but payload is clearly cut off.

Impacts:
- End-user latency increased ~120ms on average due to retries
- Throughput dropped ~8% during the window
- Error rate (500/4xx) increased by ~3.7% for streaming endpoints

We're on the latest JS client SDK (v2.3.1) and haven't changed our usage patterns. Can Redwood confirm if there were infra changes or known issues? If it's client-side, we can temporarily switch to request/response non-streaming, but that's a big lift.

Attaching:
- acme_error_sample.pcap (pcap)
- acme_stream_log.txt (sanitized)

We'd like a triage call ASAP — have availability 11:30 PDT or 13:00 PDT today.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Platform Reliability
Acme Analytics
[Attachment: acme_error_sample.pcap (pcap, 2.3MB)]
[Attachment: acme_stream_log.txt (txt, 98KB)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-20T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in partial responses from /v1/stream (production)

Thanks for the heads up — initial read of the pcap and logs suggests repeated connections where the remote side (server) sends DATA frames but the client closes the stream before the final trailer bytes are observed. Two immediate possibilities:

1) Client SDK: under certain HTTP/2 multiplexing conditions the JS SDK may emit an early 'close' when detecting a zero-length DATA frame boundary incorrectly; there was a recent opt-in change to frame coalescing in v2.3.1.
2) Network middlebox: intermittent TLS termination or proxy that is cutting the connection during high-concurrency bursts.

I'm creating a Jira to track triage and capture traces: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2048 (INF-2048). Please upload any additional traces there.

Immediate mitigation suggestions (if Acme wants quick steps):
- Switch to non-streaming / synchronous endpoints for the heaviest pipelines (short term)
- Set client max-concurrent-streams to 12 instead of default 100 to reduce multiplex pressure (config change)
- Try rolling back to SDK v2.2.7 (no frame-coalescing opt-in) to see if failure rate drops

We'll try to reproduce internally with an instrumented client. Marissa, once we have repro logs I'll propose a short patch; if that's fast we can push a customer hotfix.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Spike in partial responses from /v1/stream (production) — plan

Quick summary after initial repro attempts and the call:

What we saw:
- Reproducer using v2.3.1 of the JS client demonstrates an intermittent early close when two frames are written in rapid succession and the client-side coalescing path emits a premature close event. Not a network middlebox in initial runs.
- Failure mode: server sends final DATA chunk + trailer but client-side parser returns 'end' before trailer bytes are validated, resulting in truncated payload at the application layer.

Proposed immediate mitigation (next 24 hours):
1) Customer-side config change: set client max-concurrent-streams to 12 (low risk) — this will be communicated as a recommended workaround during the call.
2) Shipping SDK hotfix: patch the JS SDK parser to delay end-of-stream emission until trailer validation completes. Target: v2.3.2 hotfix within 18-24 hours if repro stands.
3) If hotfix is not possible quickly, offer Acme a temporary credits package tied to the measured error window and an SLA exception while patch is deployed.

Next steps assigned:
- Vivek: build & test hotfix branch and post artifacts to INF-2048 (ETA 6-8 hours)
- Marissa / Monica: prepare customer comms and credit proposal (ETA 4 hours)
- Monica: schedule follow-up with Acme after hotfix verification

I’ll escalate to leadership if we hit any blocker on the hotfix timeline. Thanks everyone for rapid triage.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
